title: The Turnoff That Is Only on the Map

features.name: the-paper-sign
features.desc-on-touch: A sign on a stick, weathered and sun-cracked, bearing directions to a place the ground beneath your feet refuses to acknowledge. The sign is real. The road is a rumour that paper started and the earth will not confirm.

features.name: the-fencepost-that-marks-nothing
features.desc-on-touch: A post driven deep, wire still attached, enclosing a boundary that only the map can see. The ground on both sides is identical. The fence knows which side it is marking, though no one else can tell.

features.name: the-cartographic-stand
features.desc-on-touch: A map case, still mounted on a post, glass long gone. Inside, the map insists: turn here. Step off the case onto the ground and find nothing but unmarked country. The map is more real than the turning.

features.name: the-traced-turning
features.desc-on-touch: The earth here is worn where footsteps refuse to land, where vehicles never quite turn. Dust settles in the shape of an intention. The ground has learned to look untouched while being infinitesimally worn.

features.name: the-grid-reference-marker
features.desc-on-touch: Coordinates painted on stone, fixing this nowhere into the paper's logic. When you stand here, you know exactly where you are not. The mesh casing bleeds a quiet signal: the archive knows this place that nothing else will verify.

inscription: the map was right; the ground forgot; the archive will remember both versions
